aws.overview: Monkey continuously assesses the security configuration of your AWS account through a read-only role. It discovers its servers, databases, storage and functions, lets you choose which ones belong to each service and turns every result into input for your controls' automated tests.
features: Discover the account's resources in the regions you declare
Choose which resources belong to each service
Assess identity and privileged access, encryption and network exposure, logging, alerts and backups
Repeat the assessment every 6 or 24 hours
See each finding with its control code, its impact and how to fix it
prerequisites: Permission in your AWS account to create an IAM role or deploy a CloudFormation template
Your AWS account number and the regions where the service runs

security_audit.name: SecurityAudit
security_audit.detail: Read the security configuration of the account's services.

view_only_access.name: ViewOnlyAccess
view_only_access.detail: List and view resources without reading the content of your data.

assume_role.name: Assume the role
assume_role.detail: Only Monkey, with your company's external ID, and for sessions of one hour at most.

security.read_only: The role cannot create, change or delete anything in your account.
security.temporary_credentials: Each assessment uses one-hour temporary credentials; with the recommended role Monkey does not store keys to your account.
security.external_id: Only Monkey, with the identifier it generates for your company, can assume the role.
security.isolated_execution: Each assessment runs in an isolated environment that is deleted when it finishes.
security.tenant_isolation: Your account's results are visible only to your company.
security.encrypted_keys: If you choose the access keys channel, they are stored encrypted and never shown.

microsoft_365.overview: Monkey assesses the security configuration of your Microsoft 365 organization with read-only access that you authorize with one button. Each result feeds the automated tests of your controls.
features: Assess identities and access: second factor, conditional access and privileged roles
See the real progress while it is assessed
Repeat the assessment every 6 or 24 hours
prerequisites: A Global Administrator (or Privileged Role Administrator) of your organization to authorize access
To review email: assign the “Global Reader” role to the Monkey application after authorizing
Some checks require Microsoft licenses: if your organization does not have them, they stay unmeasured

directory.name: Directory and roles
directory.detail: Read users, groups, who is an administrator and the synchronization with your servers. Includes data about people.

activity.name: Activity and reviews
activity.detail: Read audit and sign-in logs and access reviews.

security_signals.name: Security data
security_signals.detail: Read identity alerts and query security events. Those events may include data about people, devices or email.

devices_and_sites.name: SharePoint and managed devices
devices_and_sites.detail: Read SharePoint settings and the configuration of managed devices.

mail.name: Email
mail.detail: Lets Monkey read the email configuration according to the role you assign to the application. Assign “Global Reader”, which cannot change anything.

security.read_only: Monkey asks for read permissions. The email one acts according to the role you assign: “Global Reader” cannot change anything.
security.temporary_credentials: Each assessment uses temporary Microsoft access. Monkey stores no passwords or secrets from your organization.
security.isolated_execution: Each assessment runs in an isolated environment that is removed when it finishes.
security.tenant_isolation: Only your company sees your organization’s results.
